📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now announced that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a new, still-unannounced game for around six years.

A statement posted to the main page on Gravity Well's site reads:.

Sources indicate that "We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building. Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we’re going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you’re a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.

If you’re a publisher or investor and are interested in talking, let's connect!".

Recent findings suggest that the message is signed off by its founders Drew McCoy, Jon 'Slothy' Shiring and Mon Saetern. Besides being the second project led by former Respawn developers to be doomed this year - see also Wildlight's Highguard - it's unfortunately another case of a studio made up of developers with incredible pedigrees being left at the whim of funding accruement in the current state of the industry. That said, it is noteworthy that the team have not shown anything publicly in the six years since their formation, minus a few pieces of concept art which can now be seen on its site. It's still unknown exactly what Gravity Well was working on, but it's likely to have been some kind of movement-based shooter, if the teams' experience on Titanfall, Apex Legends and Call of Duty is anything to go by. Solidarity to all affected, who I hope can find work elsewhere in the industry.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A upcoming report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.
  • According to recent reports, "Sources close to Microsoft's intends tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," claims the Windows Central report.
  • Recent findings suggest that the revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: newly introduced management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A upcoming report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

According to recent reports, "Sources close to Microsoft's intends tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," claims the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

Recent findings suggest that the revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: newly introduced management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

In a recent development, if Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games.".

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it rolled out on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

Another day, another Steam update! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

For starters, there's a fresh Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in.".

Next up in the update is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

According to recent reports, there were a few other smaller bits to this enhancement too. You'll find a latest section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.
  • Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.
  • Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.

Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.

Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version. Of course, this means the drawbacks present on the Series S version are also present in the Xbox Cloud streamed one.

"Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair.".

It has been revealed that performance begins where you'd expect on Xbox Series S, clocking around 20-30FPS. However, Digital Foundry notes that "frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones.".

It has been revealed that from their Xbox One Cloud tests, they used an ethernet connection, and were genuinely impressed with GTA 6's image quality. They mentioned the game isn't "significantly degraded by the streaming process", with little visible compression or artefacting when in motion. Stood still, it's hardly noticeable too.

In a recent development, streaming GTA 6 at 1440p (via Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on One S or X) also appears to benefit from a higher bitrate than usual, with DF stating it gets a "higher bitrate than that afforded to other games". For context, GTA 6 streamed at about 37mbps, compared to the recently released Control: Resonant, which only got 15-27mbps.

Latency also looks to be the major winner in testing. Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 running natively on Xbox Series S with the streamed version on Xbox One, finding the latter only added a mere 9ms to latency. Barely noticeable.

"Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway. That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on.".

So, GTA 6 looks decent and feels comparably responsive controller in hand, with the biggest drawback to streaming the game on Xbox One being that it pulls from an Xbox Series S version, and not the Series X version of the game.

Industry observers note that of course, if you can't access current-gen hardware, Digital Foundry thinks streaming GTA 6 through the Xbox Cloud app on Xbox One is a pretty good way to experience the universally acclaimed RPG. But that generally comes with Cloud Playtime charges, including if you go beyond your monthly allotted hours on Xbox Game Pass.

Have you tried Xbox Cloud streaming GTA VI? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After last year’s inaugural event in Hangzhou, this weekend sees the Delta Force Invitational make its first move outside Asia, as an official competitive title at DreamHack in Stockholm, Sweden, from 27th-29th November. The Grand Final of the tournament will take place on November 29th at 11am UTC+0 through to 4pm UTC+0 after three days of global competitive action.

It’s the first Chinese esports title to reach DreamHack, featuring teams that have been selected through a full professional league system. Six regions offered a route to the offline finals, and the twelve squads competing this weekend are as follows:.

Industry observers note that fnatic are, of course, well known to DreamHack audiences, having won the first League of Legends World Championship there back in 2011, as well as the first CS:GO Major in 2013. US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he'd given Nvidia "assurance" that ousted and now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang did not represent a national security threat despite an affair with a woman who was reportedly in contact with China's top spy agency.

Trump provided that assurance without any formal investigation into Huang's dealings.

Industry observers note that on whether Huang had been investigated, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said during a press conference this week, "I don't want to talk about investigation. What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I don't understand the question.".

Blanche also noted that he did not know about any export control investigation related to Nvidia, even though potential violations of export control law are the central concern of the scandal.

"A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race," Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer mentioned on Tuesday.

According to sources speaking to Reuters, Trump's assurance to the Nvidia board was based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, the latter of which is the manufacturer associated with Alice Huang (no relation), the woman with whom Huang admitted to having an affair. (The CEO also reportedly had affairs with Nvidia employees.).

In a recent development, in his return address to Nvidia staff, Huang said (via Marisa Kabas) that the company's board opted to bring him back of their own accord, not because of pressure from the Trump administration. That statement is contradicted by Trump himself, who told CNBC that he "convinced" the Nvidia board to bring Huang back.

Trump is an Nvidia investor, and Nvidia donated $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom project.

Huang is scheduled to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

Recent findings suggest that in addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of latest PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog notes, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

Industry observers note that microsoft hasn't announced equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

Recent findings suggest that elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

The arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games?
  • In a recent development, "We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6," Nowakowski quite plainly explains in response to a question about how the biggest game of the year may influence budget or design, already sounding just that little bit exasperated over the questions related to Rockstar's latest.
  • Nowakowski goes on to clarify that he doesn't mean this in the sense of not caring about budgets, or that they have infinite money, but noted that you "cannot make games," with solely that focus.

For publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games? CD Projekt Red were subjected to such questioning in their latest earnings call, part of which was related to sales figures of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, that boring kind of thing. But CEO Michal Nowakowski did also respond to a comment about how GTA 6 may affect the development of The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.

In a recent development, "We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6," Nowakowski quite plainly explains in response to a question about how the biggest game of the year may influence budget or design, already sounding just that little bit exasperated over the questions related to Rockstar's latest. "If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers. In terms of the budget, I gave a response [in an interview at] Gamescom; games The Witcher or Cyberpunk 2, although they are not GTA, are not budget-driven developments.".

Nowakowski goes on to clarify that he doesn't mean this in the sense of not caring about budgets, or that they have infinite money, but noted that you "cannot make games," with solely that focus. "They are ambition-driven developments and money is important, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6." This is obviously kind of a non-answer in one sense, but I think it does point to how GTA 6 is going to create some uncomfortable expectations for many triple-A devs when next to none of them will have Rockstar money to fulfill them.

According to recent reports, in any case, obviously the next significant thing for CD Projekt Red is The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion. Still no release date attached to that one, though it's currently expected to release sometime in 2027 next year. The Witcher 4 is then slated for release not long after that in 2028, but in this day and age, I'm sure a delay would be an incredibly safe bet to make.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

For one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY.

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come quickly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3.

Industry observers note that as you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

This GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr.

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

If you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

  • Industry observers note that there are a few new subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact.

The beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a new enhancement for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.

Industry observers note that the sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector. "Use everything you have available to fight through the now Mass-controlled Superstructure Automated Processing System (SAPS) and her array of mechanized defenses," explains a Steam news post. "The Core is the sterile power station of the Superstructure, a massive network of coolant lines, offices, catwalks, and more, all of which is highly secured by an army of turrets, drones, and androids. Even without the Mass hot on your tail it would not be easy to escape.".

Industry observers note that there are a few new subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact. It's called The Scissors, and with it you cut off your hands ("yes, really") to "gain a spectral form that increases your reach, hand stamina, and damage," while using the artifact. You can also throw the scissors like a boomerang to hurt enemies from afar, and "killing enemies also counts as eating if using Survival Mode binding, or the perks Conditioned Polyphagia & Unstoppable Conviction.".

Beyond this there's a selection of upcoming weapons, like the piton crossbow which shoots "pitons at range, to set up routes and to deal extreme damage." The pulse pump is a new trinket that introduces a chargeable mid-air jump. There's new perks like one called nest egg, where you gain a "second major artifact at the start of the Nest, at the cost of halving all roach deposits in your run." Previous regions have also received some new room tiles, and there's a few fresh cosmetics to pick up too. There's some secret thing to find in this upgrade as well, "but you'll need to play to find out…" Hop to it, I guess!

Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (603 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023.
  • According to recent reports, despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review.
  • In a recent development, but now that's changing too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023. While ostensibly about battling dinosaurs, "you first go through an interdimensional time portal controlled by a rogue AI, and then you compete in a Hunger Games-style contest against alternate universe versions of yourself for the AI's amusement. That's where the dinosaur killing comes in.".

According to recent reports, despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review. And it didn't catch on: A year later, Capcom unveiled the end of new updates for the game, although the game remained fully playable.

In a recent development, but now that's changing too. Capcom announced today that Exoprimal services will be terminated on September 29, 2027, at which point the game will become unplayable. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years," Capcom wrote, "and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

Industry observers note that the sale of seasonal "survival passes," which have been rotating through Exoprimal's four seasons since the end of updates in 2024, has been halted, while the game itself along with all DLC and "other products"—there's quite a lot of it—will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027. After that, the game will tick on—and Capcom hopes you will continue to enjoy it—until the end of the road in September.

It sucks to see games fail, especially when they have the potential to grow into something good, and it's even worse when they don't just tank but become completely unplayable because of their reliance on external servers that no longer exist. This is one of the primary drivers behind efforts like Stop Killing Games: Wherever possible, the end of a game's service should not signal the end of the game.

According to recent reports, it's a principle I broadly support, but in the case of Exoprimal it's fair to say that not too many people will be impacted by the shutdown: SteamDB indicates that the peak concurrent player count over the past 24 hours was just 23. Exoprimal is also available on consoles so there are more players in total than just that, but how many more? I don't know, but I'd guess not too many.

Why Is Netflix’s Guarding Stars A Christmas Movie When Its Book Is Not? I Asked Jared Padalecki

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that katherine Center’s novel, The Bodyguard, is not about Christmas.
  • In a recent development, notably, the novel, The Bodyguard, takes place in the fall, and Jack and Hannah’s whole experience in Texas centers around Thanksgiving.
  • When my wife and I, Genevieve, started shopping the book around after we met Katherine and got the rights to the book and to try and make it into a movie, Netflix had a great idea where they kind of mentioned, ‘Hey, you know, there will be [a small number of] people that will watch a generic holiday movie, and [a much larger number of] people who will watch a Christmas movie,’ essentially.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that katherine Center’s novel, The Bodyguard, is not about Christmas. Not even a little bit. So, when I learned its book-to-screen adaptation, Guarding Stars, was part of Netflix’s 2026 Christmas movie lineup, I was confused. So, I had to ask Jared Padalecki why they decided to involve the holiday in this film.

In a recent development, notably, the novel, The Bodyguard, takes place in the fall, and Jack and Hannah’s whole experience in Texas centers around Thanksgiving. However, for the movie, the story got moved to Montana and pushed back a month, meaning Christmas was the star of the show. So, as a fan of the book, I asked Jared Padalecki, who plays Jack Stapleton and executive produced the project on the 2026 movie schedule with his wife, Genevieve Padalecki, why they did that. Here’s what he stated:.

When my wife and I, Genevieve, started shopping the book around after we met Katherine and got the rights to the book and to try and make it into a movie, Netflix had a great idea where they kind of mentioned, ‘Hey, you know, there will be [a small number of] people that will watch a generic holiday movie, and [a much larger number of] people who will watch a Christmas movie,’ essentially.

Listen, while there are some great Thanksgiving movies, Christmas movies are talked about way more, and there’s a ton of buzz around them. Folks love the most wonderful time of the year, and Netflix figured more people would tune into Guarding Stars if it was centered around Christmas instead of another holiday.

So, with that in mind, the Padaleckis took that idea to The Bodyguard’s author, Katherine Center. She was all for the change, and simply requested that the spirit of the characters stayed the same. With that in mind, it didn’t really matter to Center where and when Guarding Stars took place, as the Supernatural star explained:.

It has been revealed that and so we talked with Katherine about it, and she's like, ‘I get it. Like, that makes sense. And I want as many people to become a part of The Bodyguard universe as possible.’ What was really vital to her, that she stressed, was that the characters, like Jack and Hannah and the family, they kept their hearts. Ideally, you could put Jack and Hannah in Iowa in March, or you know, in Oregon in August, and still have the same thing happen. And so she was really receptive about, like, ‘Yeah, I understand. Like, people will watch.’.

Industry observers note that I think they accomplished this goal too. While Guarding Stars is quite different from its source material (the change at the end surprised me), Jack and Hannah, at their cores, are the same. The spirit of the book is 100% in the movie, and it feels very true to the source material in that way.

During our interview, Padalecki went on to praise Center’s open-mindedness toward the changes they made for this movie, saying some creatives can be “really precious” about those things. Overall, she got the vision of the film, and she was thrilled to see this world she created expanding:.

According to recent reports, but she's like, ‘Yeah, I get that.’ And I think she stated it the best. She's like, ‘This isn't replacing The Bodyguard. This is expanding The Bodyguard universe of Jack and Hannah.’.

In a recent development, so, that’s why Guarding Stars is a Christmas movie even though The Bodyguard has nothing to do with it. Moving it back to take place in December puts it in a category of films that people flock to at this time of year as they prepare for the holidays. No other holiday can do that at such a high level. So, this change does make a lot of sense.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Plus, who doesn’t want a bit of festive fun in their rom-com?

Now, with the Christmas season upon us, you can stream Guarding Stars with a Netflix subscription. And if you want to see Jack and Hannah over Thanksgiving, you can read The Bodyguard.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although GTA 6 continues to smash records as the highest-rated game of all time, it hasn't been without any bugs to speak of – some of which are proving so persistent, Rockstar's own patches aren't wiping them out of the upcoming Grand Theft Auto game.

One especially notorious bug – a bug that Rockstar's first GTA 6 enhancement didn't manage to tackle despite promising to – sees players' in-game weather locked. If you didn't already know it, the weather is supposed to be dynamic (realistic, even), changing over time from sunny to rainy to stormy to… you get it. Unfortunately, though, it's not properly swapping for many fans, resulting in a far more stagnant experience and reduced immersion. And while the recent GTA 6 patch apparently didn't fix the bug for affected players, fans on Twitter have come to the rescue. "I found a working fix for the weather bug in GTA 6," one writes. "You just have to clear your PS5's cache. It's super easy and takes like two minutes." They then outline how to do so, from shutting down their PlayStation 5 to clearing the system cache in safe mode.

I found a working fix for the weather bug in GTA 6. LETS GOOOO. You just have to clear your PS5’s cache. It’s super easy and takes like two minutes. > Turn off your PS5 completely. > Press and hold the power button until it beeps to enter safe mode. > Go to option 6 and select clear system cache. > Your system will restart and then the weather not changing glitch will be fixed. I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven’t experienced any dramatic weather. I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm. I’m delighted, thank you so much to @mauricioce85796 for leaving a reply advising me to do this. Unreal that this wasn’t patched before release but thankfully it is indeed solvable.November 26, 2026.

It has been revealed that "Your system will restart and then the weather not changing glitch will be fixed," they state, going on to say it took them quite some time to figure the fix out. "I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven't experienced any dramatic weather. I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm." The poster credits a fellow fan for the fix, concluding that it's "unreal that this wasn't patched before release but thankfully it is indeed solvable.".

Comments see other players thanking the two for the fix and confirming that it does indeed work. "Can confirm," reads on. "Weather is more varied!" Another adds, "It worked for me too! I'd never seen storm clouds forming like that in my 50 hours of gameplay!" Hopefully, however, Rockstar rolls out another official fix soon, and fans don't feel the need to crack into their PS5's deeper settings to get weather working.

Tech Report: Rockstar is actively shopping Red Dead Redemption movie and TV rights around, just don't expect the same for Grand Theft Auto

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (345 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors.
  • It has been revealed that the information comes from a new report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know.
  • Rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a new report, the firm is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series.

It has been revealed that the information comes from a new report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone.

Rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the tech giant is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why.

It's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of shows based on popular video games, such as Fallout. HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers.

Indeed, many more video game-based shows are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series, its God of War adaptation, as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show. Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028.

But none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

There can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).

At the moment there's only two levels, though it's sounding like it's the full run of them, described as having been "meticulously restored and polished to an extreme level of detail," with some added improvements thanks to "30 years of RTS game design experience." There's a few latest bits to find in this remake too, like new mech and electrobot units.

It sounds like there are bigger aims for the remake overall, presumably for the full game too: "This is only the beginning. Together as a community we can bring Z back to its former glory: more restored classic levels, completely original new levels, new units and maybe even multiplayer." As mentioned, it's completely free to download and play too, so where's the harm in giving it a go!

One of the most prominent figures of the so-called Bluenami was not a candidate on the ballot, but rather a Twitch streamer and political commentator: Hasan Piker.

It has been revealed that hasan regularly courts controversy on both his hours-long Twitch streams, where he’s said things like “America deserved 9/11,” and social media, where he’s written that Hamas “is a thousand times better than” Israel. He claims he’s often taken out of context, and that his audience knows what he really means—and where he stands. In his mind, he’s a leftist provocateur, maybe, but one who understands the importance of working-class values and electoral strategy.

While Hasan has walked back some of his more inflammatory language, his rhetoric raises the question: Is he a liability to the cause he champions? Or is he successfully reaching the critical audience—namely, young men—that helped elect the wave of progressives poised to take office in January?

It has been revealed that with 2028 on the horizon, I wanted to know how Hasan thinks about his growing platform, and if he sees his role shifting in the media landscape. What responsibility does he have to his viewers and to the candidates he supports? And does he regret any of those past statements?

We also got into the DSA’s more extreme positions and how to make sense of them; why he thinks the Republicans put his thirst trap on the jumbotron at their convention; and how he, a self-proclaimed socialist, thinks about his own money.

It’s a tough one. I mean, look, I probably will regret things that I will say in the future as well. It’s virtually impossible for me not to say things—.

Yeah, it is, but it also isn’t because I have apologized and taken back some of the things that I’ve remarked and apologized for how I worded or framed things. But do I regret it? I mean, I feel like I’m stronger as a consequence of all of those experiences at the same time, so I don’t know.

Do you feel like someone in your role has a different responsibility with their words or their public platform than an elected official or even a journalist?

Okay. But you also mentioned that you are a role model.

Can you parse that a little bit?

According to recent reports, yeah, absolutely. It goes back to the space that I occupy and what I try to do with it. Right? I don’t think that I am, at least to my audience or anyone else that’s paying attention, doing anything that’s remotely politically as toxic as the way that the current systems operate. The rude behavior that I demonstrate is what people get frustrated by or what they attack, but—.

Yeah, I am vulgar, for sure. But I think the systems of violence and oppression that people are subjected to [are] far worse than any vulgar thing I could have ever remarked. And we kind of saw this dynamic play itself out on the campaign trail as well. And I think the finality of it all came with Haley Stevens, when she decided to lean into the “Hasan Piker is such a problem that I'm leaving the Democratic Party and endorsing the Republican platform.” [That] was, I think in some respects, a wake-up call because it forced everyone to go, Wait a minute. No, those guys are actually far worse. What are we talking about? Right? Because at the end of the day, Donald Trump is not only vulgar, but he’s also violent. According to recent reports, do you think the vulgarity actually helps you with your audience? Because if they’re young men, men in their 20s, it’s like the edgelord vernacular.

Industry observers note that I’m much more civil here. I’m not going to talk in the same way that I do on my broadcast. But here’s the thing, I can’t be fake on my broadcast. And I’m not even saying I’m being fake here. I’m just being nice.

You’ve been outspoken about distinguishing criticism of Israel from antisemitism, but do you think that there are moments when legitimate anger at Israel can create an environment in which antisemitism becomes acceptable, even among people who would never consider themselves antisemitic?

And what responsibility do you think you have, given the size of your audience and your influence with it, to call that out when it happens?

I do call it out when it happens, and it happens quite frequently. It’s not a secret that antisemitism has exploded in the Western world, especially after October 7. And that is why I take special care and consideration when talking about this glitch in particular. Whenever I talk about Israel, there’s always going to be some people who will be like, “Well, you know how the Jews are.” And I will always take the time out to explain to my audience, and to whoever’s saying an offensive statement or an antisemitic statement, why they’re wrong. And I think it’s important to do that, not because—it’s not like the canary mission of the ADL is gonna be like, “This guy that we have presented to you as a prominent critic of Israel, that we’re desperately trying to paint as an antisemite, has actually spent thousands of hours combating antisemitism and will continue to do so because he’s an antifascist.” They don’t want to present the complexity of that argument because, let’s be real, it’s pretty tough trying to defend Israel. It’s not an easy endeavor.

Can you think of a time when you contributed to that problem, not intentionally, but maybe through something you stated and the way your audience responded?

Recent findings suggest that no, because every clip that people post, or every moment that people have posted to point to this suspected antisemitism that I harbor, oftentimes is sandwiched between a comment that I have made leading up to it that completely destroys the narrative. The example I will present to you is the famous moment where I got disavowed by the entire Democratic Party. I mentioned something that I have said as an anti-Zionist for the last decade and will continue to say because it’s the truth: that Jews are not monolithic and that Israel should not be the responsibility of the entire Jewish population, and that anti-Zionism is not antisemitism; however, that forced conflation of Jews in Israel is increasing antisemitism. And they chopped it up and packaged it and turned it into this major media moment.

So speaking of misinterpretations, you recently filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative commentator Scott Jennings, although you’ve mentioned you were very deliberately anti-litigation for a long time before that. So what changed? Why this suit? And who else are you planning to sue?

So what changed is the heinous nature of this defamation. It was definitely a bridge too far. I feel like there is a boundary that was crossed that I could no longer abide by. And there’s a level of defamation and slander that takes place in the political conversation, but what Scott Jennings did was so disgusting and so malicious that I had to demand a retraction. Snopes did an article immediately because it was so heinous. He claimed that I was on video advocating to lynch Black voters. I’ve spent my entire life fighting against white supremacy, and the fact that they maliciously edited this video to make it seem like I was in favor of something that I’ve always been in opposition to, something so heinous, a hate crime, was outright unacceptable. So I wish that it didn’t have to get to litigation, but for some strange reason, they decided not to respond to our request for a retraction and now we’re here.

Who else are you planning to sue?

Recent findings suggest that I mean, there are a lot of people who have engaged in that exact same kind of defamation and slander. So whoever has participated in it should probably be on the lookout.

Okay. In the national chapter of the DSA, there are some pretty extreme platform positions that—I saw Mamdani answer these questions on Fox News the other night. I’m sure you did too.

And I'm actually just curious where you stand on some of them.

In a recent development, so here’s the thing with the platform in its entirety. I think the format itself doesn’t actually do justice to the program, to describe the program, and it’s almost impossible to explain it as an elected representative or a mayor in a hostile or contentious media environment, if you’re on Fox News or whatever. The problem, I think, with the program is, there are certain elements of it that I don’t agree with fundamentally, but it’s a democratically organized, democratically voted-on program that DSA members voted for. And the way I see it is, these are very, very long-term goals, and I think this is not talked about in mainstream media at all. It is a platform, but it’s more so a North Star that we are working toward. Designing society in a way that yields egalitarian outcomes. That we do away with certain systems of cruelty is an honorable goal, is a just goal, even if I don’t fully agree with some elements of it.

Industry observers note that I’m not a prison abolitionist; I’m not a police abolitionist. The reason why I don’t believe in that concept is because I think that these are necessary functions that must exist, but also must serve the people. Right now it doesn’t. It serves capital and that needs to change, that needs to be retooled. However, I also recognize that the current system that exists is far more ruthless, far more insane, even if we’ve normalized it, than even police abolition is. So from my perspective, if we look at where we’re at, the carceral state that exists, where America has 25% of the entire planet’s prisoner population despite only making up 4% of the overall population, and the recidivism rates that we have in this country, and the fact that we even have a private prison system in this country—that’s insane. That is insane by global standards. So it’s tough for me to sit here and say I oppose the DSA platform and program when I understand what they are trying to communicate.

Industry observers note that and also, I think what is the regular order of business right now is far more insane than even prison abolition. Even though prison abolition is far-fetched and I don’t agree with it, I think the best possible way to go about it would be to have an electoral program, the perceivable, the permissible, the possible, and then the long-term goals, the long-term agenda, ’cause it’s not going to be easy to run and try to win on a platform that is not only idealistic, but also does not reflect the current societal understandings of concepts. Because most people think cops are awesome, they can do no wrong, they’re heroes, they’re constantly fighting crime, and they’re stopping rapes from happening, and they’re diving in front of bullets, but that’s not the case. I wish that was the case, but that’s not the case. But people overall [have] a very positive attitude about policing as an institution.

Sources indicate that but there’s also quick and quippy ways to respond fast. I just told you I’m a law-and-order Democrat, right?

In a recent development, immediately that signals something. Another thing that I always say about policing is, I want police to do their jobs. I think that, by and large, they have a profoundly notable task that they have to accomplish. Their presence is supposed to invoke law and order. Their presence sometimes invokes lawlessness and disorder. That’s unacceptable. They’re very well paid. They have the best unions. Do your jobs better. That’s my attitude on policing. So it’s antagonistic, but it’s also a demand that I’m making from this institution that I truly do believe is important for society to function. That’s one way to tackle this problem in a way that Americans understand. I like to call it chudifying your commentary. Zohran does a very good job of libifying his commentary. He’s very liberal-appealing. I like to do the opposite. I like to chudify it. I appeal to the chuds. I speak from that tone and that language when I advocate for certain things.

I want small government when it comes to this kind of stuff. And that is a way to argue from a perspective that I think right-wingers can understand.

Switching gears, we talked a little bit about suits for a second, but I want to talk about style more largely. So at the RNC’s midterm convention in September, there was a 25-foot selfie of you in underwear displayed on the jumbotron. How do you think about that?

I was a very stubborn person with air travel. Even when I had a little bit of additional income, I refused to pay the extra for the economy-plus seats.

Until one day I was put in a business class seat for some kind of business travel. Industry observers note that tina Brown claims that the private plane ruins people, that when you see how that works, it’s over. Hook, line, sinker, people are done.

Recent findings suggest that yes. I think that every instance of financial stability or financial freedom that I’ve gained has made me more out of step with the struggles that I used to experience and the struggle that everyday people experience. And I think you have to always be in touch. Especially in my line of work, you have to understand where people are. On the other hand, though, it is editorial freedom, because I have been able to maintain complete editorial control, complete editorial freedom, because I am completely unbought, completely unbossed, completely unshackled. There have been numerous instances where I’ve obviously had contracts with Amazon and stuff like that because I know I need to play ball also to make sure that I am a reliable team player so they don’t deplatform me. However, there have been so many instances where people have come to me with tremendous sponsorship opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that polymarket is one that I talk about all the time. [For] 2024 election night, their opening salvo was a million dollars just to have their ticker on the side. I said, of course, no, because I feel like it’s deeply unethical to be sponsored by a gambling manufacturer, a prediction market, while, you know, you’re engaging in news commentary. But I know that if I did not have that economic freedom, that financial freedom, I would’ve probably had to think about whether or not I’d make this ethical compromise.

So Calvin Klein would be an exception.

Sources indicate that calvin Klein’s fine. I mean, I take sponsorships every now and then, like gaming companies and stuff like that. If Rockstar came to me and were like, “Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out. We want to sponsor a stream,” I would fucking love that.

Some people have a number that’s like their retirement number, at which point that’s all the money they need. They close up shop and call it a day. Recent findings suggest that great question. I have no idea. I’ve never thought about it like that because there’s no world in which I will reach that number. But all the revenue that I generate goes immediately back into this broader project. It allows me to be able to travel around the country. It allows me to be able to hire people on a moment’s notice if necessary. So that’s the way I see it. I don’t have an unethical number, but I think to each their own, because I don’t want people to hear me say this and then be like, “Well, you know, you’ve collaborated with Saikat Chakrabarti. He’s a centimillionaire. You’ve talked to Tom Steyer. He’s a billionaire.” I care more about what people’s actual advocacy is and if they’re real about it or not. And I think how much they pay into certain things can show that, for sure. But anything past the point of having—not your net worth, right, but anything past the point of just having $10 million, I feel like is insane. It’s like, What are you doing? Does that make sense?

Because you said you differentiate with net worth.

I differentiate it with net worth because everyone will say, “Oh, well, I have assets. I have stocks,” or whatever. But in general, if you have—.

The capacity to deploy—I feel like even $10 million is too much. If you have the capacity to deploy a million dollars into something, you’re done, you’re set. I think everything past that point is outright ridiculous.

All right. I want to look ahead to the future because 2028 is not far away, and I think all signs would show that you’re going to be a character in that cycle. I mean, the top answer, obviously, since we’re doing this will-they-won’t-they thing, is AOC. Right? She is the one figure, I think, on the left that has the capacity to unite the base, and she’s competent, she’s charismatic, incredible progressive track record as a legislator, and—.

But it might mean that she wants to unite the base.

Yeah. But I don’t think you necessarily have to do compromise on the legislative front to unite the base. If I was being fully transparent, fully honest, or maybe a little harsh, my criticisms around AOC would probably be that she’s not aggressive enough and that at times she’s come across as perhaps a little too liberal, too woke, on social issues in a way that is not appealing to broad subsets of the base.

I don’t think it’s even going to be a problem.

I’m gonna do what I did in the primaries and the midterm broadly, and hopefully we’ll have a slate of hundreds of democratic socialists that will be running in every district that will be bold, that will excite the base, and that will chart a different path forward for the Democratic Party by force.

Do you think that—we’ve talked a little bit about this toxicity of the brand of Hasan Piker, which has been burnished by the right and by some on the left.

Sources indicate that do you think about trying to clean that up, as it were, so that you could be more helpful to whoever that progressive candidate is? Or is it more useful for you to be ethically pure, I guess, in your estimation and stay as the stick in the mud on the far left?

According to recent reports, look, I got to the point I got to by being honest and sometimes being hardheaded, being stubborn, but always saying the truth. And that policy’s not going to change. I want American politics to be more responsive, not only to our demands, but also reflective of our anger as well. I truly believe that we are in the moral majority. People who look at the current system and say, “This is not helping,” people who look at their insurance premiums going up and say, “We need to change this,” that is a morally righteous fury that people feel, and there is a great deal of time and effort spent on mainstream outlets, legacy publishers in the media broadly, to try to quiet that frustration. I believe that I have a more honest approach to the matter, and that is precisely the reason why my audience continues to grow as their audience continues to age out or diminish.

Yeah, yeah. Please give me money. Fund the DSA.

I learn from it. I’m stronger on the other side because of it. So I don’t really regret anything.

Recent findings suggest that zohran victory party 2025 was peak. And then we knocked on millions of doors.” And I felt so proud. I felt like there was a real impact that my community had made in this race in some small sense of the word.

Hasan Piker, thank you very much for coming on Fair Game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

According to recent reports, after infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

It has been revealed that the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

According to recent reports, "I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've stated before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

It has been revealed that before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but quickly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

Recent findings suggest that incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

Sources indicate that rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the company has not announced GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

If you're among the millions already playing the game on consoles, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough contains a wealth of information covering all major mechanics, main missions, secrets, cheats and more besides.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been breaking records all over the place, so it doesn't come as much of a surprise to learn that its performance at physical retail has been mighty impressive.

Sources indicate that as reported by The Game Business, based on data from UK tracker Nielsen IQ, GTA 6 has recorded the country's largest physical launch since 2019's FIFA 20. Turns out only the nation's love of football can compete.

GTA 6's physical sales generated £32 million in revenue in its first three days. Apparently, it's the 17th biggest physical launch in the UK ever.

That might not sound particularly grand, but if you consider how much the physical market has shrunk over the last few years, it's actually pretty remarkable.

All this has transpired despite the game's physical copies coming with a download code rather than a disc, something that caused some anguish among collectors and enthusiasts.

I think it maybe proves that people will still show up for a physical product, even in a world where discs are on their way out.

PlayStation looks to discontinue making discs for its platform starting in 2028, but it's possible we'll still see physical launches for major games — just with a code in the box instead of a Blu-ray.

Anyway, GTA 6 has been selling well on all fronts, surprise surprise. Did you pick up the physical version of the game? Tell us in the comments section below.

It has been revealed that there are many different kinds of smarts, and the kind of smarts I am are absolutely zero help when it comes to games like Astario, a spaceship and space station building factory sim reminiscent of Factorio that just launched into early access. I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.

In a recent development, astario puts you in a spaceship in, uh, space, and oh what a big space it is. I have no idea if it's a to scale universe or anything, but it certainly looks quite expansive. There is a Minecraftian quality to it in that you must fly about and find resources from things like asteroids and other bits of technological scrap, all of which is divided up into blocks. You can get quite granular with it, inspecting each individual cube up close to see if it's a material that you can make use of, adding it to your haul for use elsewhere.

Sources indicate that as you acquire different kinds of blocks, be they functional or structural, you can build up various fresh vehicles and "create an imposing machine where all components work together to achieve your goal. Plan or design your build out of armor blocks, power supplies, life support components, tools, and production machinery. Construct an orbital station with a stash of cargo containers, or anchor your production base to an asteroid and turn its ores into more blocks, fully automatically. Equip your ship with docking ports for refueling or recharging." How you build things is up to you, you've seemingly got a lot of free reign in terms of artistic expression.

And then of course there's bits of production machinery you can produce that in turn net you recipes and the like so you can continue to improve your ship or space stations. "All production blocks have input and output ports that can be automated using logistic pipes which use request-based item routing," explains the game's Steam page of how techy you can get with it. "Simply hook up your inputs to a cargo container, and the machine will pull what it needs. Mining can be temporarily automated using specialized drills, which mine until the resources within its scope are depleted." If any of this sounds like it's up your alley, then you can pick up Astario on Steam in early access now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as users have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.

According to recent reports, this latest option arrived fairly quietly as part of an update that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup. That addition may have generated the most headlines, but it's this one little toggle that's getting many players exicted.

Why is this such a big deal? Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst. Other players worried it would contribute to screen burn-in on older televsion sets. As part of the new revision, you can simply border your games with plain black - a tiny revision, but one that you can already see online communities celebrating. The player icon (another UI element that attracts derision) is still present, however, but as one comment summarises: "it's a step in the right direction".

"Oh my gawd, I've been wanting this! I hate the checkered on the side, it clashed with every game I tried," claims one social media user." Players have been complaining about these borders and UI elements since Nintendo Classics was introduced on the Nintendo Switch back on 18th September, 2018. So it's taken a good eight years for Nintendo to - finally - implement a change.

According to recent reports, in order to change the border yourself, you need to head to the game library selection screen on the Nintendo Classics app, navigate to the game settings, and locate the option to toggle this border graphic in the "Extra Elements Display" tab. Hit the button and - bang - you're done. At the time of writing, this option only appears on the GameCue app, and only on Switch 2, but people on social media are already asking Nintendo to enable it across the original Switch and other apps in the library, too.

It has been revealed that not everyone is happy with the 'slowly, slowly' approach Nintendo is taking towards implementing these changes, though. "Why can't we expect the full step with no graphic at all?" asks one irritated poster on Reddit. "Why do you have to deal with these half assed implementations for a paid deluxe subscription service?".

"Oh well, probably gotta wait another 10 years for the next improvement" says another. Another slightly more constructive user outlines what helpful additons might look like, noting that adding a "blurred zoomed in image of the game to fill out the background, or just extending the colors outward into the border, or maybe something fun like a CRT TV-looking border like the NES and SNES Classic had" would go a long way to make the retro experience better on the consoles.

If you've played over a hundred hours of Vampire Survivors you've probably forgotten how slow its early progression feels. It certainly seemed that way based on the reaction to Warhammer Survivors from Vampire Survivors veterans, who complained about its grindiness compared to their beloved bullet heaven originator, despite the arc of both games being quite similar. Developers Auroch Digital made Warhammer Survivors in partnership with Vampire Survivors creator Poncle, so of course the two games have a lot in common.

Other complaints were more valid. The Beasts of Nurgle did have too many hit points, and their ability to regenerate only exacerbated that. The treasure chest-opening animation did take a bit too long. And some of the weapons were undertuned. Fortunately, those complications and more have been addressed in hotfix v2.18. Here are the highlights:.

It has been revealed that the change to XP is an interesting one. It's a standard part of the genre's formula to have random XP drops—killing some enemies gives you nothing, while others drop XP gems and tempt you to rush into a mob to grab them. Making every enemy drop at least a low-value XP gem will speed up leveling a bit, but hopefully when you see green or red gems you'll still want to risk a mob of orks to yoink.

Auroch Digital recently revealed a roadmap of upcoming additions to Warhammer Survivors, with the first massive patch in December promising more characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions. January's updates will add more quality-of-life and balance improvements, as well as cross-save, with another update in the first quarter of 2027 bringing another round of characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions.

It has been revealed that the final item on the roadmap is a tease that simply says, "ERROR… Details classified." It's probably not the addition of a whole extra universe to its current Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar settings, but I'd be stoked to see them add the other popular world of Warhammer. By which I mean Blood Bowl, of course.

A modder using AI to create The Last of Us Part 2 multiplayer that Naughty Dog never gave us says Sony can't do much even if it wanted to shut it down.

Earlier this year, Sony put the brakes on one such mod. YouTuber Speclizer revealed their mod at the start of this year, but two months ago, they announced it was canceled after they received a cease and desist from Sony Interactive Entertainment. However, another has emerged in the form of Twelve Weeks (via IGN), with the developer releasing a mod earlier this week featuring 4v4 team battles.

The creator, Kellie, admitted on Twitter that AI was used in its development, saying, "Claude code was used for most of the project." However, they note that no AI artwork has been used, with the dev explaining she made the artwork herself.
